chapter_theme: Friendships that don't fit: with those who stay only for their own ends, whose bond is shallow, who are of another nature, or who lack discernment. Such friendship fades, pains, and drags down even the discerning, while the company of the wise is like heaven.

231.reading: Lord of the well-watered hills where waterfalls pour from dark peaks, like people who stay under an old leaking roof, making mud dams and bailing out and catching the water, some stay by you only until their own business is done.
231.nuance: The simile is of discomfort put up with for one's own sake: they stay as one stays under a bad roof, because they need it for now. Shanmuganar adds that they pretend to share one's troubles.

232.reading: Lord of the land of white waterfalls, the friendship of the excellent is of surpassing worth and fruitful like rain; that of the worthless, even at its height, is like rain that has failed.

233.reading: Enjoying the company of people of fine understanding is as desirable as the heavenly world; being joined to profitless people without understanding of subtle learning is one of the hells.

234.reading: Lord of the hills whose slopes are lined with long sandal groves, the bond with those who have no real tie seems to grow, then, like fire in straw, dies without lasting even a moment.
234.nuance: Mudaliar glosses பந்தம் as the bond of love; Shanmuganar as true attachment.

235.reading: Saying 'we will do it' of what cannot be done, and putting off what can be done, bring suffering at once even to those who have truly scorned the enjoyment of pleasure.
235.nuance: 'Even to ascetics' means these faults hurt whatever one's indifference to pleasure. The verse doesn't mention friends; only its place in this chapter suggests these are marks of an unfit friend.

236.reading: Though born in the same pool and growing up together, the water-lily never equals the spreading kuvalai; so though they gain the friendship of the large-natured, the deeds of those who lack that nature remain different.
236.nuance: Pope's title speaks of a lotus; the Tamil compares the ஆம்பல் with the குவளை, the blue water-lily.

237.reading: Lord of the hills where the unripe little monkey, with fingers like dry bean-pods, pokes and prises at the father who meets it to snatch his food, the friendship of those not of one mind with you is painful.
237.nuance: The image is of closeness without regard: the young monkey takes from the one nearest to it.

238.reading: If, when my friend is in distress, I do not hurry to put my precious life in his hands, may I go where the man who violated his friend's guarded wife goes, while the world of lasting words laughs.
238.nuance: The chapter on unfit friendship includes this vow of what a fit friend owes. Mudaliar names the destination as hell and gives three readings of நெடுமொழி வையம்.

239.reading: Lord of the good hills where honey flows, leaving the friendship of those who know what is good to befriend the petty-minded is like emptying cow's ghee from a vessel and filling it with neem oil.

240.reading: One fitted for good form who lacks generosity toward his town is like milk fit to drink mixed with water; the discerning taking up with bad company is like a cobra mating with a female viper.
240.nuance: Mudaliar records the belief that a cobra mating with a viper dies, so the image predicts ruin.

positions.position: உருவிற்கு அமைந்தான் is first one with some qualities fit for greatness; Mudaliar gives good looks only as another view.
It is one handsome in form, as Pope also has it.

links.note: Both describe friends who stay while there is something to gain. 812 asks what it matters whether one keeps or loses them; 231 shows them putting up with discomfort until their business is done.
284 has crowds gathering like crows while wealth lasts and no one asking after you when it goes; 231 shows the same self-interest from inside the friendship.
Both say the friendship of the worthless is barren even at its fullest. 811 says it is better shrinking than growing; 232 says even at its height it is like failed rain.
Both set the company of the learned against heaven. 137 doubts heaven could be sweeter; 233 makes the comparison explicit and adds that bad company is one of the hells.
Both put the company one keeps at the extremes: no greater support than good company and no greater affliction than bad (460), heaven and hell (233).
Both describe a friendship that seems to grow and then shrinks: the moon past full (782), fire in straw (234).
818 says to let slip the friendship of those who make difficulties of what they could do. 235 names the same delay, with empty promising, and says it brings suffering even to ascetics.

177 says the smallness of the small stops showing when they join the great, as water in milk looks like milk. 236 says their deeds stay different though they grow up beside the great. Read together, association changes how the small look, not what they do.

Both say an outside good doesn't change an inner nature: 823 says the unworthy rarely become good at heart however many good books they study, and 236 says the same of their friendship with the large-natured.
Both make inner accord the condition of friendship. 825 says not to trust the words of those not one with you in mind; 237 says friendship with them is painful.
787 says friendship shares the suffering when ruin comes. 238 raises the stake to one's own life and curses the friend who holds back.
797 calls leaving the friendship of fools a gain. 239 describes the reverse exchange, leaving the discerning for the petty-minded, as ghee swapped for neem oil.

240 says the discerning who take up with bad company are ruined; 244 says the good-natured don't turn bad in mind though their company is bad. On Mudaliar's reading of 240 as ruin, the two fit: such men may keep their minds and still lose everything else, as 180 says of the sandal tree in a forest fire.
Both say bad company ruins the good: 179 compares it to a storm wrecking a ship, and 240 to a cobra mating with a viper.

source_issues: 233: the Tamil has a corrupted character (நுண்ணு஡ல் for நுண்ணூல்).
240: Pope's text ends with a separator line, and the shanmuganar field ends with a section header labelled இன்ப இயல் for chapter 25, though chapter 25 is listed under பொருட்பால்.
